previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of CNS diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and diabetes insipidus was admitted with acute right flank pain. Imaging revealed a 5 mm right UPJ stone causing mild hydronephrosis and acute kidney injury, with creatinine rising to 1.7. He also presented with hyponatremia (sodium 125), attributed to excessive desmopressin use. He was managed with IV fluids, pain control, and underwent cystoscopy with right ureteroscopy, laser lithotripsy, and stent placement. His creatinine improved to baseline (1.1) and sodium normalized with reduced desmopressin dose and fluid restriction. Topiramate was downtitrated due to nephrolithiasis risk, lamotrigine was increased, and lisinopril was discontinued during acute kidney injury. He was discharged home with stable renal function, a ureteral stent pending outpatient removal, and follow-up scheduled with urology and neuro-oncology.
problems: Hydronephrosis with renal and ureteral calculous obstruction
Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, extranodal and solid organ sites
